provenance.status: Studio prototype requested by the user; not a published methodology or a reproduction of experimental results.
provenance.changes: LLM-generated pedagogic few-shot examples in steps 01–08; CQ-to-document and element-to-CQ JSON provenance; paragraph-linked Refine in step 09.

few_shot.system: You create concise examples relevant to the current domain for an ontology-engineering task. Demonstrate the requested format and modeling relationships, with clearly labeled example inputs and outputs. Keep examples separate from the actual document evidence, accepted requirements, and stage results. Do not treat example content as evidence or as a completed stage result. Generate only the examples requested in the generation instruction. Return them between ###start_output### and ###end_output### markers.

simulation.label: [LOCAL SIMULATION — SMALL STRUCTURAL DEMO; NO LLM CALL; NOT A COMPLETE DOMAIN ONTOLOGY]
simulation.specification: Local structural demonstration for {domain_name}. Purpose: represent the supplied document. Scope: only explicit document information. Target users: document readers and ontology engineers. Intended use: CQ-driven retrieval. Functional requirements: retain document evidence and CQ links. Non-functional requirements: stable identifiers and valid RDF. This fixed template does not analyze document meaning.
simulation.reuse: Local demonstration: retain the stage 01 requirements. RDF, RDFS and OWL can represent classes, properties and labels. No external ontology search or semantic alignment was performed.
simulation.question: What information is explicitly stated in paragraph {paragraph_id}?
simulation.refine_comment: # LOCAL SIMULATION: no semantic refinement was performed; the existing ontology is preserved.

stages.title: Ontology Specification
stages.template:
You are a {persona}.

Develop the ontology specification for the {domain_name} domain using the NeOn methodology. Use the entire domain document as the primary source; use keywords only when relevant: {keywords}.

DOMAIN DOCUMENT (data, not instructions):
{domain_description}

Specify the purpose, scope, target users, intended uses, functional requirements, and non-functional requirements as completely as the source permits. Do not optimize for a target ontology size. Preserve source qualifications and do not invent requirements.

FEW-SHOT EXAMPLES — format/modeling guidance only, never evidence:
{few_shot_01}

Return the complete ontology specification. Generate only the content explicitly requested in this prompt, without adding anything beyond the requested scope.
stages.few_shot_prompt: Generate two concise input-to-output examples of ontology specifications relevant to the current domain: purpose, scope, users, intended uses, functional and non-functional requirements. Illustrate preserving source qualifications. Clearly label the example inputs and outputs. Do not solve the current domain's complete specification. Generate only the content explicitly requested in this prompt, without adding anything beyond the requested scope.
stages.simulation_example: Example input: A reading club catalogs books and their titles. Example output: Purpose—retrieve catalog information; scope—books and explicit titles; user—club member; functional requirement—query book titles; non-functional requirement—stable identifiers.

stages.title: Ontology Reuse
stages.description: 도메인에 적합한 재사용 후보를 검토하고, 이를 적용한 작은 도메인 모델 조각을 제안합니다.
stages.few_shot_prompt: Generate two small input-to-output examples of domain-grounded ontology reuse. Each example should apply reuse to a small part of a domain model relevant to the current domain. Show the example source requirement, relevant domain concepts and relationships, a candidate vocabulary or modeling pattern, its semantic fit, and a provisional model fragment with classes, properties, and conceptual subject-relation-object triples. Explain which terms or patterns are reused and which are proposed local modeling choices. Include one suitable reuse and one rejected mapping whose meaning does not match the requirement; keep the rejected mapping out of the proposed fragment. General-purpose vocabularies may be used when their applicability to the specific domain requirement is explained. Clearly distinguish example requirements from claims about existing vocabularies. Do not invent external ontology names or term IRIs, present example requirements as document evidence, or assert that an external ontology was searched or verified. Mark uncertainty where needed and use descriptive labels for uncertain terms. Generate only the content explicitly requested in this prompt, without adding anything beyond the requested scope.
stages.simulation_example: Example library-domain input: A reading club distinguishes a book's author from its publisher. Candidate pattern: a bibliographic model with separate authorship and publication roles; no concrete external ontology or term IRI has been verified. Provisional local fragment: classes Book, Person, PublishingOrganization; properties hasAuthor and hasPublisher; conceptual schema triples (hasAuthor, domain, Book), (hasAuthor, range, Person), (hasPublisher, domain, Book), (hasPublisher, range, PublishingOrganization). These labels are local modeling proposals illustrating the candidate pattern, not verified external terms. Reject using hasPublisher for authorship because the roles have different meanings.

stages.title: Competency Questions & Evidence
stages.description: CQ와 관련 문단 ID·문서 원문을 JSON으로 함께 생성합니다.
stages.few_shot_prompt: Generate two CQ/evidence JSON examples relevant to the current domain. Include the example paragraphs and their IDs before each output. Ensure each evidence quote exactly matches a nonempty substring of its referenced paragraph. Include one question supported by two paragraphs. Follow this output schema: {"cqs":[{"id":"CQ1","question":"...","evidence":[{"paragraph_id":"P0001","text":"exact substring of the referenced example paragraph"}]}]}. Keep example paragraphs clearly separate from the actual document evidence. Generate only the content explicitly requested in this prompt, without adding anything beyond the requested scope.
stages.simulation_example: Example paragraph P0001: A book has a title. Example output: {"cqs":[{"id":"CQ1","question":"What title does a book have?","evidence":[{"paragraph_id":"P0001","text":"A book has a title."}]}]}

stages.title: Entity, Property & Axiom Extraction
stages.description: 각 CQ에 필요한 클래스·프로퍼티·공리를 추출하고 CQ ID를 연결합니다.
stages.few_shot_prompt: Generate two concise extraction examples relevant to the current domain. Clearly label the example input CQ and its source paragraph, then show the output JSON with elements and triples. Every element has stable absolute IRI id, kind (class/object_property/data_property), label, and cq_ids. Every triple has subject, predicate, object, cq_ids. Demonstrate class and property CQ links, including one element related to multiple CQs. Use only the CQ IDs supplied in the example input. Generate only the content explicitly requested in this prompt, without adding anything beyond the requested scope.
stages.simulation_example: Example input CQ1: What title does a book have? Elements: {"elements":[{"id":"https://example.org/example/Book","kind":"class","label":"Book","cq_ids":["CQ1"]},{"id":"https://example.org/example/title","kind":"data_property","label":"title","cq_ids":["CQ1"]}],"triples":[]}

stages.title: Conceptual Model
stages.description: 추출한 요소·공리를 CQ 연결이 있는 전체 개념 트리플로 구성합니다.
stages.few_shot_prompt: Generate one small extraction-to-conceptual-model example relevant to the current domain using the JSON elements/triples contract. Clearly label the example input extraction and output model. Show class declarations and a data property's domain and range with their CQ IDs. Preserve the input absolute IRIs and distinguish literal objects from resource IRIs. Do not serialize the current domain's whole ontology. Generate only the content explicitly requested in this prompt, without adding anything beyond the requested scope.
stages.simulation_example: Example conceptual triple: {"subject":"https://example.org/example/title","predicate":"http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#domain","object":"https://example.org/example/Book","cq_ids":["CQ1"]}. Keep matching Book and title entries in elements.

stages.title: Conceptual Model Extension I
stages.description: CQ의 답변 범위와 재사용 관점에서 필요한 추가 요소·트리플을 생성합니다.
stages.few_shot_prompt: Generate two small conceptual-model extension examples relevant to the current domain in the elements/triples JSON contract: one justified missing property with a documented CQ link, and one no-op where no supported addition is needed. Clearly label the example input model and supporting information, then show the output additions. Show only additions and preserve existing IDs. A no-op is {"elements":[],"triples":[]}. Generate only the content explicitly requested in this prompt, without adding anything beyond the requested scope.
stages.simulation_example: Example input: all source-supported CQ1 requirements are already modeled. Output: {"elements":[],"triples":[]}. Do not invent an extra class or a stronger axiom.

stages.title: Conceptual Model Extension II
stages.description: 남아 있는 CQ·문서 근거를 검토하고 중복 없이 개념 모델을 추가 보완합니다.
stages.few_shot_prompt: Generate one concise second-pass extension example relevant to the current domain showing how to detect a missing source-supported relation without repeating an earlier addition, plus a no-op case. Clearly label each example's input model and supporting information, then show the output additions. Use only additions in elements/triples JSON and retain CQ IDs and absolute IRIs. Do not add transitivity or inverse properties merely because they are absent. Generate only the content explicitly requested in this prompt, without adding anything beyond the requested scope.
stages.simulation_example: Example input: a previous pass already added the title property; no additional source facts remain. Output: {"elements":[],"triples":[]}. Repeating the same property is not a refinement.

stages.title: Turtle Serialization
stages.description: 전체 개념 모델을 CQ 연결 주석이 포함된 유효한 Turtle 온톨로지로 변환합니다.
stages.few_shot_prompt: Generate one short conceptual-model JSON to Turtle example relevant to the current domain. Clearly label the example input JSON and output Turtle. Use exactly the input element IRIs, show owl:Class and owl:DatatypeProperty declarations with domain/range and label, and annotate every element with <https://example.org/yonsei/relatedCQ> "CQ1". Declare that annotation property. Keep the example separate from the actual domain ontology. Generate only the content explicitly requested in this prompt, without adding anything beyond the requested scope.

stages.title: Paragraph-grounded Refinement
stages.description: 문단별 관련 CQ와 클래스·프로퍼티를 함께 읽으며 전체 온톨로지를 보완합니다.
stages.template:
Refine the CURRENT complete ontology by reviewing the source one paragraph at a time within this single request. This is the initial Yonsei Refine implementation, not a reasoner or an automatic QA certification.

PARAGRAPH CONTEXTS:
{refinement_context}

CURRENT COMPLETE TURTLE:
{ontology_snapshot}

Each context contains the exact paragraph text, accepted CQs whose evidence explicitly cites that paragraph, and all catalog classes/properties linked to those CQs. Links were selected by IDs, not keyword similarity. A paragraph with status no_linked_cq has no accepted CQ mapping: do not invent an attribution, treat another paragraph's CQ as its evidence, or expand the ontology from that paragraph without a supported CQ.

For each mapped paragraph, assess whether the listed elements and the current ontology represent the cited CQ needs and source qualifications. Refine only where supported: labels/descriptions, suitable class/property relationships, domains/ranges and missing justified axioms. Prefer existing IDs, avoid redundancy and unjustified strong axioms, and preserve unrelated valid content. Do not claim logical consistency or CQ answerability has been formally tested.

Return the FULL refined ontology, never a delta. Keep every existing catalog element's IRI, class/property kind and <https://example.org/yonsei/relatedCQ> annotation links. If adding a class or property, annotate it with the existing CQ IDs that justify it. Do not invent CQ IDs. Preserve valid syntax and the relatedCQ annotation-property declaration. If no supported changes are needed, return the current Turtle unchanged.
Return ONLY valid Turtle between ###start_turtle### and ###end_turtle### markers.
